mechanism_narrative: A housing starts level (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average signals strengthening demand, leading to positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns as investors anticipate improved corporate earnings and economic growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the Federal Funds Rate below 0.5% initiates a monetary easing cycle that reduces discount rates and stimulates economic activity, resulting in positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS falls below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 8%), a decline in the unemployment rate over the past month signals improving labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as economic growth accelerates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 8% and UNRATE declines by more than 0.2 percentage points in the prior month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and an increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a supply shock that is being absorbed by the labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as the economy adjusts without a deep recession.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO declines and PAYEMS increases, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 450,000 units signals a weakening in the housing market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as the economy faces a prolonged downturn.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST falls below 450,000 units, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) relative to its 12-month moving average signals improving inflation expectations, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns as the economy moves toward recovery.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL is above its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market recovery, leading to positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns as consumer spending and corporate profits rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases and UNRATE declines, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a low retail sales growth regime (RSAFS growth rate < 0.5% per month), a rise in retail sales growth above 0.5% per month signals a recovery in consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns as consumer spending accelerates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS growth rises above 0.5% in a low growth regime, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
